sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- SECTION 5: BAYES' THEOREM & CONDITIONAL PROBABILITY…
- SECTION 6: MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD ESTIMATION (MLE)…
- SECTION 7: HYPOTHESIS TESTING…
- SECTION 8: CENTRAL LIMIT THEOREM (CLT)…
- Test sensitivity (true positive rate): 90%
- Test specificity (true negative rate): 95%
- If test is positive, what's probability of disease?
- P(Test+) using law of total probability

```python
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy import stats
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = (12, 8)

print("="*80)
print("PROBABILITY & STATISTICS PART 2: INFERENCE & ESTIMATION")
print("="*80)

"""
================================================================================
SECTION 5: BAYES' THEOREM & CONDITIONAL PROBABILITY
================================================================================

VISUAL INTUITION:
-----------------
Medical Test Example:

                    Disease
                   /      \
              Yes /        \ No
               1%          99%
               /            \
        Test+/  \Test-  Test+/  \Test-
         90%    10%     5%     95%

Prior P(Disease) = 0.01
Evidence: Test is positive
Posterior P(Disease | Test+) = ?

SIMPLE EXPLANATION:
-------------------
Bayes' Theorem updates beliefs based on new evidence:

Before evidence (Prior) + Evidence → After evidence (Posterior)

P(A | B) = P(B | A) · P(A) / P(B)

"Probability of A given B" = (likelihood × prior) / normalization

REAL-WORLD USE CASES:
---------------------
• Spam Detection: P(Spam | Words)
• Medical Diagnosis: P(Disease | Symptoms)
• Recommendation: P(Like | User History)
• Search: P(Relevant | Query)

KEY CONCEPTS:
-------------
1. Conditional Probability:
   P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B)
   "Probability of A, given that B occurred"

2. Bayes' Theorem:
   P(A | B) = P(B | A) · P(A) / P(B)
   
   Components:
   - P(A | B): Posterior (what we want)
   - P(B | A): Likelihood (evidence given hypothesis)
   - P(A): Prior (initial belief)
   - P(B): Evidence (normalizing constant)

3. Law of Total Probability:
   P(B) = Σ P(B | Aᵢ) · P(Aᵢ)

4. Independence:
   P(A | B) = P(A) if A, B independent
   P(A ∩ B) = P(A) · P(B)

MATH:
-----
Bayes for Multiple Hypotheses:

P(Hᵢ | E) = P(E | Hᵢ) · P(Hᵢ) / Σⱼ P(E | Hⱼ) · P(Hⱼ)

This is the foundation of:
• Naive Bayes Classifier
• Bayesian Networks
• Bayesian Inference
"""

print("\n" + "="*80)
print("SECTION 5: BAYES' THEOREM & CONDITIONAL PROBABILITY")
print("="*80)

# Example: Medical Test
# Disease prevalence: 1%
# Test sensitivity (true positive rate): 90%
# Test specificity (true negative rate): 95%
# If test is positive, what's probability of disease?

prior_disease = 0.01
sensitivity = 0.90  # P(Test+ | Disease)
specificity = 0.95  # P(Test- | No Disease)
false_positive_rate = 1 - specificity  # 0.05

# P(Test+) using law of total probability
p_test_positive = (sensitivity * prior_disease + 
                   false_positive_rate * (1 - prior_disease))

# Bayes' Theorem
posterior_disease = (sensitivity * prior_disease) / p_test_positive

print(f"\nMedical Test Example:")
print(f"  Prior P(Disease) = {prior_disease:.2%}")
print(f"  P(Test+ | Disease) = {sensitivity:.2%}")
print(f"  P(Test- | No Disease) = {specificity:.2%}")
print(f"\nAfter positive test:")
print(f"  Posterior P(Disease | Test+) = {posterior_disease:.2%}")
print(f"\n🎯 Despite positive test, only {posterior_disease:.1%} chance of disease!")
print(f"   Why? Disease is rare (1%), false positives are common (5%)")

# Visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))

# Plot 1: Tree diagram
axes[0, 0].text(0.5, 0.95, 'Population', ha='center', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold',
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='lightblue'))
axes[0, 0].text(0.2, 0.70, f'Disease\n{prior_disease:.1%}', ha='center', fontsize=12,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='lightcoral'))
axes[0, 0].text(0.8, 0.70, f'No Disease\n{1-prior_disease:.1%}', ha='center', fontsize=12,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='lightgreen'))

# Disease branch
axes[0, 0].text(0.1, 0.40, f'Test+\n{sensitivity:.0%}', ha='center', fontsize=10,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='red', alpha=0.5))
axes[0, 0].text(0.3, 0.40, f'Test-\n{1-sensitivity:.0%}', ha='center', fontsize=10,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='white', alpha=0.5))

# No disease branch
axes[0, 0].text(0.7, 0.40, f'Test+\n{false_positive_rate:.0%}', ha='center', fontsize=10,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='orange', alpha=0.5))
axes[0, 0].text(0.9, 0.40, f'Test-\n{specificity:.0%}', ha='center', fontsize=10,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='white', alpha=0.5))

# Draw lines
axes[0, 0].plot([0.5, 0.2], [0.90, 0.75], 'k-', linewidth=2)
axes[0, 0].plot([0.5, 0.8], [0.90, 0.75], 'k-', linewidth=2)
axes[0, 0].plot([0.2, 0.1], [0.65, 0.45], 'k-', linewidth=1.5)
axes[0, 0].plot([0.2, 0.3], [0.65, 0.45], 'k-', linewidth=1.5)
axes[0, 0].plot([0.8, 0.7], [0.65, 0.45], 'k-', linewidth=1.5)
axes[0, 0].plot([0.8, 0.9], [0.65, 0.45], 'k-', linewidth=1.5)

axes[0, 0].text(0.5, 0.15, f'Posterior: P(Disease | Test+) = {posterior_disease:.1%}', 
                ha='center', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold',
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='yellow'))

axes[0, 0].set_xlim(0, 1)
axes[0, 0].set_ylim(0, 1)
axes[0, 0].axis('off')
axes[0, 0].set_title('Bayes Theorem: Medical Test', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')

# Plot 2: Prior vs Posterior
probabilities = ['Prior\nP(Disease)', 'Posterior\nP(Disease | Test+)']
values = [prior_disease, posterior_disease]
colors = ['lightblue', 'red']

bars = axes[0, 1].bar(probabilities, values, color=colors, alpha=0.7, 
                       edgecolor='black', linewidth=2)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Probability', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Updating Beliefs with Evidence', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].set_ylim(0, 0.20)
for bar, val in zip(bars, values):
    height = bar.get_height()
    axes[0, 1].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, height + 0.01, 
                    f'{val:.1%}', ha='center', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

axes[0, 1].annotate('', xy=(1, posterior_disease), xytext=(0, prior_disease),
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', lw=3, color='green'))
axes[0, 1].text(0.5, 0.10, 'Evidence\nincreases\nbelief 15.4×', ha='center', fontsize=10,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='lightyellow'))

# Plot 3: Spam Classification Example
# P(Spam) = 0.3
# Word "FREE" appears in 60% of spam, 5% of ham
prior_spam = 0.3
p_free_given_spam = 0.60
p_free_given_ham = 0.05

p_free = p_free_given_spam * prior_spam + p_free_given_ham * (1 - prior_spam)
posterior_spam = (p_free_given_spam * prior_spam) / p_free

axes[1, 0].barh(['Ham\n(Not Spam)', 'Spam'], 
                [1-prior_spam, prior_spam], 
                color=['lightgreen', 'lightcoral'], alpha=0.7, 
                edgecolor='black', linewidth=2, label='Prior')
axes[1, 0].barh(['Ham\n(Not Spam)', 'Spam'], 
                [1-posterior_spam, posterior_spam], 
                left=[0, 0], alpha=0.5, 
                edgecolor='black', linewidth=2, label='Posterior (given "FREE")', 
                color=['lightgreen', 'lightcoral'])

axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Probability', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_title('Spam Detection: P(Spam | "FREE")', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].legend(fontsize=10)
axes[1, 0].text(0.5, 1.5, f'Prior: {prior_spam:.0%} → Posterior: {posterior_spam:.0%}',
                fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', ha='center',
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='yellow'))

# Plot 4: Effect of Prior
priors = np.linspace(0.001, 0.5, 100)
posteriors = (sensitivity * priors) / (sensitivity * priors + 
                                        false_positive_rate * (1 - priors))

axes[1, 1].plot(priors, posteriors, linewidth=3, color='blue', label='Posterior')
axes[1, 1].plot(priors, priors, '--', linewidth=2, color='gray', alpha=0.5, label='Prior (reference)')
axes[1, 1].axvline(prior_disease, color='red', linestyle=':', linewidth=2, label=f'Our case ({prior_disease:.1%})')
axes[1, 1].axhline(posterior_disease, color='red', linestyle=':', linewidth=2, alpha=0.5)
axes[1, 1].scatter([prior_disease], [posterior_disease], s=200, c='red', zorder=5)

axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Prior P(Disease)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Posterior P(Disease | Test+)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_title('How Prior Affects Posterior', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].legend(fontsize=10)
axes[1, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('bayes_theorem.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\n✓ Saved Bayes' Theorem visualization")

print(f"\nSpam Example:")
print(f"  Prior P(Spam) = {prior_spam:.0%}")
print(f"  After seeing 'FREE': P(Spam | 'FREE') = {posterior_spam:.0%}")

"""
================================================================================
SECTION 6: MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD ESTIMATION (MLE)
================================================================================

VISUAL INTUITION:
-----------------
You flip a coin 10 times: H T H H H T H H T H (7 heads, 3 tails)

What's the best estimate for P(Heads)?

Likelihood function:
L(p) = p^7 · (1-p)^3

        L(p)
         ▲
         │     ┌─┐
         │    ╱   ╲
         │   ╱     ╲
         └──┴───────┴──→ p
           0   0.7  1    ← Maximum at 0.7!

MLE: p̂ = 0.7 (just the empirical frequency!)

SIMPLE EXPLANATION:
-------------------
MLE finds parameter values that make observed data most likely:

Given data, what parameters make it most probable?

Steps:
1. Write likelihood function L(θ | data)
2. Take log: log L(θ)
3. Find maximum: d/dθ log L = 0
4. Solve for θ̂

REAL-WORLD USE CASES:
---------------------
• Estimate mean/variance of data
• Fit probability distributions
• Train logistic regression
• Estimate neural network weights

KEY CONCEPTS:
-------------
1. Likelihood Function:
   L(θ | x₁,...,xₙ) = P(x₁,...,xₙ | θ)
   = ∏ᵢ P(xᵢ | θ) (if independent)

2. Log-Likelihood:
   ℓ(θ) = log L(θ) = Σᵢ log P(xᵢ | θ)
   (Easier to work with!)

3. MLE:
   θ̂_MLE = argmax_θ L(θ | data)
   
4. Properties:
   - Consistent: θ̂ → θ_true as n → ∞
   - Asymptotically normal
   - Efficient (low variance)

MATH:
-----
For Bernoulli trials (n heads, m tails):
L(p) = p^n · (1-p)^m
ℓ(p) = n log(p) + m log(1-p)
dℓ/dp = n/p - m/(1-p) = 0
→ p̂ = n/(n+m)

For Normal distribution:
μ̂ = (1/n)Σxᵢ (sample mean)
σ̂² = (1/n)Σ(xᵢ - μ̂)² (sample variance)
"""

print("\n" + "="*80)
print("SECTION 6: MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD ESTIMATION (MLE)")
print("="*80)

# Example 1: Coin flip MLE
np.random.seed(42)
true_p = 0.7
n_flips = 100
flips = np.random.binomial(1, true_p, n_flips)
n_heads = np.sum(flips)
n_tails = n_flips - n_heads

# MLE estimate
p_mle = n_heads / n_flips

print(f"\nCoin Flip Experiment:")
print(f"  True P(Heads) = {true_p}")
print(f"  Observed: {n_heads} heads, {n_tails} tails")
print(f"  MLE estimate: p̂ = {p_mle:.3f}")

# Likelihood function
p_values = np.linspace(0.01, 0.99, 200)
likelihood = p_values**n_heads * (1-p_values)**n_tails
log_likelihood = n_heads * np.log(p_values) + n_tails * np.log(1-p_values)

# Example 2: Normal distribution MLE
true_mu, true_sigma = 5, 2
samples = np.random.normal(true_mu, true_sigma, 200)

# MLE estimates
mu_mle = np.mean(samples)
sigma_mle = np.std(samples, ddof=0)  # MLE uses n, not n-1

print(f"\nNormal Distribution Experiment:")
print(f"  True μ = {true_mu}, σ = {true_sigma}")
print(f"  MLE estimates: μ̂ = {mu_mle:.3f}, σ̂ = {sigma_mle:.3f}")

# Visualizations
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))

# Plot 1: Likelihood function for coin
axes[0, 0].plot(p_values, likelihood, linewidth=2.5, color='blue')
axes[0, 0].axvline(p_mle, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'MLE: p̂ = {p_mle:.3f}')
axes[0, 0].axvline(true_p, color='green', linestyle=':', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'True: p = {true_p}')
axes[0, 0].scatter([p_mle], [p_mle**n_heads * (1-p_mle)**n_tails], 
                   s=200, c='red', zorder=5)
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Parameter p', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Likelihood L(p | data)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_title(f'Likelihood Function: Bernoulli ({n_heads}H, {n_tails}T)', 
                     fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[0, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 2: Log-likelihood (easier to visualize)
axes[0, 1].plot(p_values, log_likelihood, linewidth=2.5, color='purple')
axes[0, 1].axvline(p_mle, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'MLE: p̂ = {p_mle:.3f}')
axes[0, 1].axvline(true_p, color='green', linestyle=':', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'True: p = {true_p}')
axes[0, 1].scatter([p_mle], [n_heads * np.log(p_mle) + n_tails * np.log(1-p_mle)], 
                   s=200, c='red', zorder=5)
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Parameter p', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Log-Likelihood ℓ(p | data)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Log-Likelihood (Easier to Maximize)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[0, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 3: Fitted normal distribution
axes[1, 0].hist(samples, bins=30, density=True, alpha=0.6, color='skyblue', 
                edgecolor='black', label='Data')

# True distribution
x_range = np.linspace(samples.min(), samples.max(), 200)
true_pdf = stats.norm.pdf(x_range, true_mu, true_sigma)
axes[1, 0].plot(x_range, true_pdf, linewidth=3, color='green', 
                linestyle=':', label=f'True: N({true_mu}, {true_sigma}²)')

# MLE distribution
mle_pdf = stats.norm.pdf(x_range, mu_mle, sigma_mle)
axes[1, 0].plot(x_range, mle_pdf, linewidth=3, color='red', 
                linestyle='--', label=f'MLE: N({mu_mle:.2f}, {sigma_mle:.2f}²)')

axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('x', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_title('MLE for Normal Distribution', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[1, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 4: Convergence of MLE with sample size
sample_sizes = [10, 50, 100, 500, 1000]
estimates_mu = []
estimates_sigma = []

for n in sample_sizes:
    sample = np.random.normal(true_mu, true_sigma, n)
    estimates_mu.append(np.mean(sample))
    estimates_sigma.append(np.std(sample, ddof=0))

axes[1, 1].plot(sample_sizes, estimates_mu, 'o-', linewidth=2, markersize=8, 
                label='μ̂ (MLE)', color='blue')
axes[1, 1].axhline(true_mu, color='blue', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, alpha=0.5)
axes[1, 1].plot(sample_sizes, estimates_sigma, 's-', linewidth=2, markersize=8, 
                label='σ̂ (MLE)', color='red')
axes[1, 1].axhline(true_sigma, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, alpha=0.5)
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Sample Size (n)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Estimate', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_title('MLE Convergence: More Data → Better Estimates', 
                     fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[1, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
axes[1, 1].set_xscale('log')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('maximum_likelihood.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\n✓ Saved MLE visualization")

"""
================================================================================
SECTION 7: HYPOTHESIS TESTING
================================================================================

VISUAL INTUITION:
-----------------
Null Hypothesis H₀: "No effect" (e.g., μ = 0)
Alternative H₁: "There is an effect" (e.g., μ ≠ 0)

           H₀ Distribution
              ▲
           ┌──┴──┐
          ╱       ╲
         ╱         ╲
    ────┴───────────┴────→
       -2σ    0    +2σ
        ├─────────────┤ ← 95% of data
        │             │
     Reject H₀    Reject H₀
     (too low)    (too high)

If observed data falls in rejection region → Reject H₀

SIMPLE EXPLANATION:
-------------------
Statistical test answers: "Is this effect real or just random chance?"

1. Assume H₀ is true (no effect)
2. Compute probability of seeing data this extreme
3. If probability < α (e.g., 5%) → Reject H₀
4. Conclude: effect is statistically significant

REAL-WORLD USE CASES:
---------------------
• A/B Testing: Is new design better?
• Drug Trials: Does drug work?
• ML Models: Is accuracy improvement significant?
• Feature Selection: Is feature useful?

KEY CONCEPTS:
-------------
1. Null Hypothesis (H₀):
   Status quo, "no difference"
   
2. Alternative Hypothesis (H₁):
   What we want to prove
   
3. Test Statistic:
   Measure of how far data deviates from H₀
   
4. p-value:
   P(data as extreme as observed | H₀ is true)
   Small p-value → Reject H₀
   
5. Significance Level (α):
   Threshold for rejection (typically 0.05)
   
6. Types of Errors:
   - Type I: Reject true H₀ (false positive)
   - Type II: Fail to reject false H₀ (false negative)
   
7. Power:
   P(Reject H₀ | H₁ is true) = 1 - P(Type II error)

COMMON TESTS:
-------------
• t-test: Compare means
• z-test: Large sample mean test
• Chi-square: Categorical data
• ANOVA: Compare multiple groups
• F-test: Compare variances

MATH:
-----
t-statistic: t = (x̄ - μ₀) / (s/√n)

where:
- x̄ = sample mean
- μ₀ = hypothesized mean
- s = sample std dev
- n = sample size

Critical value at α=0.05: |t| > 1.96 (large n)
"""

print("\n" + "="*80)
print("SECTION 7: HYPOTHESIS TESTING")
print("="*80)

# Example: t-test
# H₀: μ = 0 (no effect)
# H₁: μ ≠ 0 (there is an effect)

np.random.seed(42)
true_mean = 2.5  # True effect
sample_size = 50
data = np.random.normal(true_mean, 5, sample_size)

# Compute test statistic
sample_mean = np.mean(data)
sample_std = np.std(data, ddof=1)
t_statistic = (sample_mean - 0) / (sample_std / np.sqrt(sample_size))

# p-value (two-tailed)
df = sample_size - 1
p_value = 2 * (1 - stats.t.cdf(abs(t_statistic), df))

# Critical value at α=0.05
alpha = 0.05
critical_value = stats.t.ppf(1 - alpha/2, df)

print(f"\nt-Test Example:")
print(f"  H₀: μ = 0 (no effect)")
print(f"  H₁: μ ≠ 0 (there is effect)")
print(f"\n  Sample mean: {sample_mean:.3f}")
print(f"  Sample std: {sample_std:.3f}")
print(f"  t-statistic: {t_statistic:.3f}")
print(f"  p-value: {p_value:.4f}")
print(f"  Critical value (α=0.05): ±{critical_value:.3f}")
print(f"\n  Decision: {'Reject H₀' if p_value < alpha else 'Fail to reject H₀'}")
print(f"  Conclusion: {'Statistically significant!' if p_value < alpha else 'Not significant'}")

# Visualizations
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))

# Plot 1: Null distribution with rejection regions
x_range = np.linspace(-4, 4, 500)
null_dist = stats.t.pdf(x_range, df)

axes[0, 0].plot(x_range, null_dist, linewidth=2.5, color='blue', label='H₀ distribution')
axes[0, 0].fill_between(x_range[x_range < -critical_value], 0, 
                        null_dist[x_range < -critical_value], 
                        alpha=0.3, color='red', label='Rejection region')
axes[0, 0].fill_between(x_range[x_range > critical_value], 0, 
                        null_dist[x_range > critical_value], 
                        alpha=0.3, color='red')
axes[0, 0].axvline(t_statistic, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'Observed t = {t_statistic:.2f}')
axes[0, 0].axvline(critical_value, color='red', linestyle=':', linewidth=2, alpha=0.7)
axes[0, 0].axvline(-critical_value, color='red', linestyle=':', linewidth=2, alpha=0.7)
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('t-statistic', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_title(f't-Test (α=0.05, two-tailed)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].legend(fontsize=10)
axes[0, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 2: p-value visualization
axes[0, 1].plot(x_range, null_dist, linewidth=2.5, color='blue')
mask_pvalue = (x_range >= abs(t_statistic)) | (x_range <= -abs(t_statistic))
axes[0, 1].fill_between(x_range[mask_pvalue], 0, null_dist[mask_pvalue], 
                        alpha=0.5, color='yellow', label=f'p-value = {p_value:.4f}')
axes[0, 1].axvline(t_statistic, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'Observed t = {t_statistic:.2f}')
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('t-statistic', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_title('p-value = P(|t| ≥ observed | H₀)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].legend(fontsize=10)
axes[0, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 3: Type I and Type II errors
null_mean, alt_mean = 0, 2
null_std = 1
x_range2 = np.linspace(-3, 5, 500)
null_curve = stats.norm.pdf(x_range2, null_mean, null_std)
alt_curve = stats.norm.pdf(x_range2, alt_mean, null_std)
critical_val = 1.645  # One-tailed test

axes[1, 0].plot(x_range2, null_curve, linewidth=2.5, color='blue', label='H₀: μ=0')
axes[1, 0].plot(x_range2, alt_curve, linewidth=2.5, color='green', label='H₁: μ=2')
axes[1, 0].axvline(critical_val, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label='Critical value')

# Type I error (α)
mask_type1 = x_range2 >= critical_val
axes[1, 0].fill_between(x_range2[mask_type1], 0, null_curve[mask_type1], 
                        alpha=0.4, color='red', label='Type I error (α)')

# Type II error (β)
mask_type2 = x_range2 < critical_val
axes[1, 0].fill_between(x_range2[mask_type2], 0, alt_curve[mask_type2], 
                        alpha=0.4, color='orange', label='Type II error (β)')

axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Test Statistic', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_title('Type I vs Type II Errors', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].legend(fontsize=9)
axes[1, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 4: Power analysis (sample size effect)
effect_size = 0.5
sample_sizes_power = np.arange(10, 201, 10)
powers = []

for n in sample_sizes_power:
    # Cohen's d effect size
    ncp = effect_size * np.sqrt(n)  # Non-centrality parameter
    critical = stats.t.ppf(1 - alpha/2, n-1)
    power = 1 - stats.nct.cdf(critical, n-1, ncp) + stats.nct.cdf(-critical, n-1, ncp)
    powers.append(power)

axes[1, 1].plot(sample_sizes_power, powers, linewidth=2.5, color='purple')
axes[1, 1].axhline(0.8, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label='Target power = 0.8')
axes[1, 1].fill_between(sample_sizes_power, 0, powers, alpha=0.3, color='purple')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Sample Size (n)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Statistical Power', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_title(f'Power vs Sample Size (Effect size = {effect_size})', 
                     fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[1, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
axes[1, 1].set_ylim(0, 1)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('hypothesis_testing.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\n✓ Saved hypothesis testing visualization")

"""
================================================================================
SECTION 8: CENTRAL LIMIT THEOREM (CLT)
================================================================================

VISUAL INTUITION:
-----------------
Roll 1 die: Uniform distribution (flat)
     ┌─┬─┬─┬─┬─┬─┐
     1 2 3 4 5 6

Average of 2 dice: Starting to look normal
        ┌──┐
      ┌─┴──┴─┐
     ┌┴──────┴┐

Average of 30 dice: Beautiful bell curve!
         ┌───┐
        ╱     ╲
       ╱       ╲
      ╱         ╲
     ┴───────────┴

THIS IS MAGIC! No matter what you start with (even dice),
averages become normal!

SIMPLE EXPLANATION:
-------------------
Central Limit Theorem: The average of many random variables
approaches a normal distribution, regardless of original distribution!

Key points:
• Works for ANY distribution
• Larger n → Better approximation
• n ≥ 30 is usually enough
• Mean of averages = original mean
• Variance of averages = original variance / n

REAL-WORLD USE CASES:
---------------------
• Why normal distribution is everywhere!
• Confidence intervals for means
• Sample surveys
• Quality control
• A/B test analysis

WHY IT MATTERS FOR ML:
----------------------
• Justifies using normal assumptions
• Foundation of statistical inference
• Explains why errors are often normal
• Allows us to quantify uncertainty
• Makes hypothesis testing possible

MATH:
-----
If X₁, X₂, ..., Xₙ are i.i.d. with E[Xᵢ]=μ, Var(Xᵢ)=σ²

Then: X̄ = (X₁+...+Xₙ)/n

As n→∞: X̄ ~ N(μ, σ²/n)

Or standardized: (X̄ - μ)/(σ/√n) ~ N(0, 1)

Standard Error: SE = σ/√n
"""

print("\n" + "="*80)
print("SECTION 8: CENTRAL LIMIT THEOREM")
print("="*80)

# Demonstrate CLT with different distributions
np.random.seed(42)
n_samples = 10000
sample_sizes = [1, 2, 5, 30]

# Original distribution: Exponential (very skewed!)
lambda_exp = 1
true_mean = 1 / lambda_exp
true_std = 1 / lambda_exp

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))
axes = axes.ravel()

for idx, n in enumerate(sample_sizes):
    # Generate samples and compute means
    sample_means = []
    for _ in range(n_samples):
        sample = np.random.exponential(1/lambda_exp, n)
        sample_means.append(np.mean(sample))
    
    sample_means = np.array(sample_means)
    
    # Plot histogram
    axes[idx].hist(sample_means, bins=50, density=True, alpha=0.6, 
                   color='skyblue', edgecolor='black', label='Sample means')
    
    # Overlay theoretical normal
    x_range = np.linspace(sample_means.min(), sample_means.max(), 200)
    theoretical_normal = stats.norm.pdf(x_range, true_mean, true_std/np.sqrt(n))
    axes[idx].plot(x_range, theoretical_normal, linewidth=3, color='red', 
                   linestyle='--', label='Theoretical N(μ, σ²/n)')
    
    # Original distribution for n=1
    if n == 1:
        original_pdf = lambda_exp * np.exp(-lambda_exp * x_range)
        axes[idx].plot(x_range, original_pdf, linewidth=2, color='green', 
                      linestyle=':', label='Original Exp(1)')
    
    axes[idx].set_xlabel('Sample Mean', fontsize=12)
    axes[idx].set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=12)
    axes[idx].set_title(f'CLT: n = {n}' + (' (Original)' if n==1 else ''), 
                       fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
    axes[idx].legend(fontsize=9)
    axes[idx].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    
    # Statistics
    observed_mean = np.mean(sample_means)
    observed_std = np.std(sample_means)
    theoretical_std = true_std / np.sqrt(n)
    
    axes[idx].text(0.05, 0.95, 
                   f'Mean: {observed_mean:.3f}\n' +
                   f'Std: {observed_std:.3f}\n' +
                   f'Theory: σ/√n = {theoretical_std:.3f}',
                   transform=axes[idx].transAxes,
                   fontsize=10, verticalalignment='top',
                   bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='wheat', alpha=0.8))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('central_limit_theorem.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\n✓ Saved Central Limit Theorem visualization")

print(f"\nCLT Demonstration (Exponential → Normal):")
print(f"  Original distribution: Exponential(λ={lambda_exp})")
print(f"  True mean: μ = {true_mean:.2f}")
print(f"  True std: σ = {true_std:.2f}")

for n in sample_sizes:
    print(f"\n  Sample size n={n}:")
    print(f"    Expected SE = σ/√n = {true_std/np.sqrt(n):.4f}")
    print(f"    Shape: {'Exponential (skewed)' if n==1 else 'More normal' if n < 30 else 'Nearly perfect normal!'}")

print("\n🎯 Key Insight: Even from exponential (highly skewed),")
print("   averages become normal with n=30!")

print("\n" + "="*80)
print("PROBABILITY & STATISTICS PART 2 COMPLETE!")
print("="*80)
print("\nKey Takeaways:")
print("✓ Bayes' Theorem: Update beliefs with evidence")
print("✓ MLE: Find parameters that maximize likelihood")
print("✓ Hypothesis Testing: Is effect real or random?")
print("✓ CLT: Averages are always normal (magic!)")
```
